model: Diversified financial (wealth/asset management + insurance) FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; net income after growth-capital retention, net debt zero)

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: fcf_*_cagr use GAAP net income (FY2020 1,534; FY2022 3,149; FY2025 3,563) as the distributable-earnings proxy, the same substitution used for NAB.AX/IAG.AX cash earnings. equity_3yr_cagr (19.9%) is an artefact of the FY2022 base being unusually depressed (equity fell to $3,803m in 2022 after $1,978m of buybacks against $3,149m of net income, i.e. a trough from which any recovery reads as a high CAGR); equity_5yr_cagr (1.3%) from the less distorted FY2020 base is the more representative figure and is the one flagged below.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case blended average of the 10-year growth path (7.0% year 1 tapering to 3.5% terminal), set between the strong 3/5-year revenue CAGRs (9.6-9.7%, flattered by the current equity-market cycle and record wrap-asset growth) and a more conservative structural rate reflecting decelerating AWM net inflows (-59% YoY in Q1 2026) and persistent Columbia Threadneedle net outflows (~$6.5bn/quarter).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (1.3%) diverges more than 30% from revenue (9.6%) and EPS (24.4%) CAGRs. This is not a red flag on data quality -- it is the central fact of AMP's model: book value is held deliberately flat-to-down because ~90%+ of earnings are distributed via buybacks and dividends rather than retained, which is exactly why the valuation uses FCFE-at-cost-of-equity rather than BVPS compounding (see inputs.notes).

scenario_narratives.base: AMP compounds revenue at 7% fading to 3.5%, as the Huntington Bank onboarding (260 advisors, ~$28bn assets) more than offsets the Comerica wind-down and record wrap-asset growth (+19% YoY) and advisor productivity (+12% YoY) continue, while organic net inflows keep decelerating and Columbia Threadneedle keeps bleeding ~$6.5bn/quarter in outflows even as AUM grows on market appreciation. Pretax margin holds near 25.5-26.5% and the business distributes ~90% of net income as dividends and buybacks (capital retained only to fund the growth a 50% ROE requires). At a 9.7% cost of equity the franchise is worth materially less than the price the market pays for a business compounding EPS at low-double-digits through buybacks alone.
scenario_narratives.bull: Huntington overshoots, further institutional wins follow, the advisor-recruiting war becomes a moat rather than a threat as AI tools widen AMP's productivity lead, Columbia Threadneedle turns net-inflow positive, and a sustained equity bull market lifts AUM/AUA broadly. Revenue grows 10% fading to a 5% terminal rate and pretax margin expands to 28%, with ROE near 53%. Even this case may not close the full gap to market price at a 9.7% cost of equity if the market is capitalising the buyback-driven EPS growth at a materially lower implied return.
scenario_narratives.bear: The advisor-recruiting war claims more large teams than it wins, the Comerica-Huntington transition slips, Columbia Threadneedle outflows widen against passive competition, and a broad equity-market correction cuts AUM-linked fee revenue precisely when RPS spread income is also squeezed by falling rates. Revenue stalls at 0-2% growth for several years and pretax margin compresses to ~20-21% before stabilising; the company keeps distributing the large majority of a much smaller earnings base rather than cutting the payout, but the earnings base itself is impaired.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AMP is a capital-light, fee-based financial (wealth management, asset management, insurance/annuities) that distributes the large majority of its earnings rather than retaining them in book value -- shares outstanding have fallen 47% over ten years while book value has been roughly flat, so a BVPS-compounding model would be measuring the wrong thing. The flow that matters is net income after the (small) capital AMP needs to retain to fund organic growth at its ~50% return on equity, discounted at a 9.7% USD cost of equity, with net debt held at zero because the balance sheet's investable assets are client, policyholder and third-party AUM, not a shareholder cash pile. This is the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity answer, the same construction used for NAB.AX, IAG.AX and MQG.AX.
key_risks_to_valuation: Equity-market beta: the large majority of AWM and Asset Management revenue is asset-based (wrap fees, AUM management fees); a sustained market drawdown directly cuts both segment revenues and reported AUM/AUA growth simultaneously with the flow pressures already present

Advisor attrition: the 'extremely aggressive'/'irrational' recruiting environment already cost AMP an $8.1bn advisor team in 2026; sustained attrition of productive advisors is a direct threat to the AWM growth engine the base case assumes continues

Institutional-channel concentration: the Comerica-to-Huntington transition (guided complete by Q3-26/early-27) is the single largest swing factor in year-1 growth; a slipped timeline or a lost future institutional relationship (as Comerica was, following its acquisition by Fifth Third) directly moves the base case

Asset-management net outflows: Columbia Threadneedle's persistent ~$6.5bn/quarter outflows are a structural headwind the model assumes continues rather than reverses; a bull-case reversal is the single largest driver of the bull/base gap
Variable-annuity and rate sensitivity: RPS pretax earnings already fell ~9% in H1-2026 on cumulative VA outflows; a sustained rate-cutting cycle compresses spread income further

Share count basis: the engine holds shares flat and compounds value through retained earnings rather than modelling the actual buyback-driven share count decline; this is a modelling convention (see inputs.share_count_basis), not a forecast that buybacks stop

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 422.37-572.56.
data_sources.financials: AMP_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, USD millions, SEC XBRL-derived, FY2006-FY2025 annual + quarterly/half-year) exported from AMP.duckdb; kpis table for buybacks, cash_taxes, interest_income; SEC XBRL companyconcept/companyfacts API (CIK 0000820027) for Revenues, NetIncomeLoss, IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest, IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit, StockholdersEquity, WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, PaymentsOfDividends -- pulled directly since AMP is a US filer with no PDF/Extracted text corpus (SEC filings are iXBRL, parsed via the XBRL pipeline per CLAUDE.md).
data_sources.qualitative: AMP_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): business model and segment revenue mix, competitive position and moat factors, growth drivers, business/financial/regulatory/macro risks, recent developments (Q2 2026 earnings, Huntington/Comerica transition, advisor attrition), FY2026 guidance.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: TTM revenue through Q2-2026 = FY2025 18,911 - H1-2025 8,971 + H1-2026 9,899 = 19,839 (SEC XBRL us-gaap:Revenues, CIK 0000820027). FY0 is a trailing-twelve-month reconstruction, not FY2025, so year 1 of the projection (Q3-2026 through Q2-2027) is one year from the valuation date, matching the engine's end-of-year discounting.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30) = 92.9m. Cover-page basic shares outstanding at 2026-07-24 were 88.33m and falling ~1.6m/quarter on the buyback pace (H1-2026 buybacks $1,653m at ~$470/share average = ~3.5m shares); the diluted weighted-average figure is used for consistency with the diluted EPS the historical growth rates are built from. Held FLAT in the projection: SBC is expensed in the flows (see sbc_source) and the buyback pace is already the mechanism by which FCFE reduces the count in reality, but the engine's per-share output divides by a flat count and grows the per-share value through retained-earnings compounding instead, avoiding a double-count of the same capital return through both a shrinking count and a discounted dividend.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction, same convention as NAB.AX, IAG.AX and MQG.AX. AMP is not a bank but the flow being capitalised (net income less capital retained for growth) is already after financing cost, and the company's investable assets (the ~$1.8T of AUM/AUA, the separate-account and general-account insurance portfolios) are client and policyholder assets or fee-generating third-party assets, not a treasury cash pile available to shareholders -- adding them back would double-count. total_debt is an approximate order-of-magnitude figure only: AMP's modern long-term-debt XBRL tags (LongTermNotesPayable, NotesPayable, LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsIncludingCurrentMaturities) are stale or missing post-2020 in the SEC concept API; the last populated combined figure was $3.0-3.3bn (2019-2020, DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount). Recorded for audit only -- it plays no role in the valuation because net_debt=0.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY0 FCFE = TTM GAAP net income (pretax margin 25.46% x (1 - 21.85% effective tax) on TTM revenue 19,839 = 3,948; ties to TTM NetIncomeLoss 3,948 = FY2025 3,563 - H1-2025 1,643 + H1-2026 2,028) less capital retained for growth. reported_fcf = last_fcf + sbc_incl_equity_taxes so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds by construction (AMP discloses no separate net-share-settlement tax line).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: AMP's own operating/free cash flow (H1-2026 OCF 3,345, FY2025 OCF 8,323) is dominated by separate-account and general-account investment-portfolio and policyholder-liability movements and is not a meaningful proxy for distributable equity cash flow, the same reason NAB's and IAG's statutory OCF was set aside. reported_fcf here is the pre-SBC FCFE proxy: last_fcf + sbc.
inputs.sbc_source: Stock-based compensation FY2025 $206m (StockBasedComp, AMP_Metrics.csv), TTM estimate 206 x 1.05 = 218 (SBC has grown roughly in line with headcount/compensation cost each year, e.g. FY2024 193 -> FY2025 206, +6.7%). 1.09% of TTM revenue (19,839); the house/street band is narrow for this reason.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped separately. Net investment income on the general account and net interest on client cash/banking balances are core parts of the AWM and RPS revenue lines (the qualitative Analysis JSON: 'net interest on client cash/banking products' inside AWM, spread income inside RPS) and are already inside base_revenue and the margin path; no separate cash pile is added to equity value (matching-asset rule).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks $2,907m (kpis, AMP.duckdb); H1-2026 $1,653m (+26% YoY vs H1-2025 $1,311m), running at ~$3.3bn annualised. This is the actual mechanism by which per-share value has compounded (shares outstanding fell 184.2m FY2015 -> 98.2m FY2025, -47%), but the engine models a flat share count with earnings retained/compounded instead -- see share_count_basis. buyback_cash is recorded for audit/cross-check only and does not feed the projection.
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total shareholders' equity $6,366m at 2026-06-30 (us-gaap:StockholdersEquity). GAAP ROE on TTM net income / average equity (6,549 FY2025-end, 6,366 Q2-2026-end) = 3,948 / 6,458 = ~61%. Management's own 'adjusted operating ROE' (Q2 2026: 55%, up from 51.5% a year earlier) runs below the GAAP figure because adjusted operating earnings exclude some GAAP-favourable items (net realized investment gains, DAC/DSIC unlocking); the model uses a more conservative 50% (base) / 53% (bull) / 44% (bear) ROE in the retention formula rather than the GAAP 61%, i.e. below even management's own adjusted figure.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.1 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 9.7%. Beta 1.1 reflects AMP's revenue being predominantly asset/market-linked (wrap and AUM fees move with equity markets, similar to a diversified asset manager) plus some insurance/rate sensitivity in RPS, modestly above a pure fee-collector's beta of 1.0. One rate across all three scenarios; flow, recruiting and market-cyclicality risk is charged in the bear flows and the probability weight, not stacked as a further premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial relative to a $6.4bn equity base and are inside operating expenses / the modelled pretax margin. No separate lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial; AMP's consolidated NCI is small (legacy joint-venture and fund-seed positions) and is absorbed in the tax/NCI-leakage allowance embedded in the cash_tax_rate_path, the same convention as NAB.AX and IAG.AX. No separate NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: SKILL.md routes 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book' to BVPS compounding x exit P/B, but AMP's book value is actively shrinking by design (equity 5yr CAGR only 1.3%, shares outstanding down 47% over 10 years) because ~90%+ of adjusted operating earnings are distributed via buybacks and dividends (H1-2026 capital return $1.9bn = 91% of operating earnings, per the Analysis JSON) -- there is very little retained book value to compound. This is the same capital-light, high-ROE, high-payout pattern as NAB.AX, IAG.AX and MQG.AX (all run as 'bank/insurer FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, engine route' rather than literal BVPS compounding), so FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROE) is the more faithful clean-surplus equivalent here too: it capitalises what the business can actually distribute after funding organic growth, rather than assuming retained earnings accumulate in book value the company has already signalled it will buy back down. Engine mapping: revenue = TTM total GAAP revenue; ebitda_margin_path = pretax income margin PLUS stock-based compensation, as % of revenue (FY0 25.46% pretax + 1.09% SBC = 26.55%, i.e. TTM pretax income 5,052 + SBC 218 = 5,270 / 19,839); sbc_pct_path = 1.09% (roughly flat -- SBC has moved in a narrow 1.0-1.1% of revenue band for a decade); da_pct = 0 (no separate D&A line disclosed outside the pretax-margin build; depreciation of AMP's own fixed assets is immaterial to a fee-based/spread-based financial); capex_pct_path = capital retained to fund growth = net-income margin x g / ROE (base ROE 50%, bull 53%, bear 44%); cash_tax_rate_path = ~22% (TTM effective tax rate 21.85%, us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit / pretax income); wacc = cost of equity 9.7%; net_debt = 0. FY0 reconciliation: 19,839 x (26.55% - 1.09%) x (1 - 22%) = 3,943, versus the TTM GAAP net income figure of 3,948 (last_fcf before the growth-capital retention deduction) -- ties within rounding.

bear.growth_rationale: The 'extremely aggressive'/'irrational' advisor-recruiting environment the Analysis JSON flags claims further large teams (an $8.1bn team already departed in 2026), the Comerica outflow is not fully offset by Huntington on the guided timeline, Columbia Threadneedle net outflows widen as passive competition intensifies, and a broad equity-market correction simultaneously cuts AUM-linked fee revenue and reported AUM/AUA growth (the Analysis JSON's own macro risk). Revenue is flat to down in years 1-2, recovering only to a 2% terminal rate as flow pressure persists structurally.
bear.margin_rationale: Pretax margin compresses to 21.0% in year 1 and 19.5% in year 2 as recruiting-economics inflation and channel-transition costs are not offset by growth, RPS spread income is squeezed by a rate-cutting cycle, and a market drawdown cuts AUM-linked fee revenue faster than costs can be cut; recovers only to a 21% mature pretax margin (no assumption of a return to the 43-44% Columbia Threadneedle outperformance); +1.1% SBC add-back.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NI margin (~16% mature) x g / ROE(44%, still well above cost of equity but below the base/bull cases as market-linked fee compression and RPS spread pressure erode returns). At 0% growth (year 2) no capital is retained; the flow is close to 100% distributable, consistent with AMP maintaining its payout policy through a downturn rather than cutting it, as management has signalled with the continued elevated H1-2026 payout ratio even amid flow headwinds.

base.growth_rationale: Revenue (TTM basis). Year 1 (Q3-26 to Q2-27) 7.0%: Huntington onboarding (260 advisors, ~$28bn assets, Q4-26/early-27) more than offsets the Comerica wind-down (~$19bn, substantially complete by Q3-26) by the company's own guidance, record wrap assets (+19% YoY) and advisor productivity (+12% YoY) continue, partially offset by decelerating organic net inflows (Q1-26 net inflows -59% YoY) and persistent Columbia Threadneedle outflows (~$6.5bn/quarter). Tapers to 3.5% terminal, below the 9.6-9.7% trailing CAGR, reflecting that recent growth has been flattered by a strong equity-market cycle (AUM/AUA +14% YoY) that will not compound indefinitely, and by the structural net-outflow drag in both AWM and asset management.
base.margin_rationale: Pretax income margin + SBC (1.09%, held flat). FY0 26.55% (TTM actual). Year 1 dips slightly to 25.2% pretax (26.3% incl. SBC) on Huntington/Comerica channel-transition costs and continued 'irrational' advisor-recruiting economics the Analysis JSON flags as a margin risk, then recovers as Columbia Threadneedle's net pretax margin (already 43-44% vs its own 35-39% target) and AWM's record advisor productivity offset the transition cost, settling at a mature 25.5% pretax (26.6% incl. SBC) -- below the H1-2026 actual of 26.1% pretax, i.e. the model does not assume the current margin-expansion trend continues indefinitely.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to fund revenue growth without shrinking the ROE base = net-income margin x growth / ROE(50%). At 7.0% year-1 growth and 19.5% NI margin, 2.73% of revenue (~10% of net income retained, ~90% distributed -- consistent with the disclosed H1-2026 91% payout ratio). Falls to 1.39% of revenue (~7% of net income retained, ~93% distributed) at the 3.5% terminal growth rate.

bull.growth_rationale: Huntington onboarding overshoots guidance and further large institutional wins follow; advisor recruiting stabilises as AI-enabled productivity tools widen AMP's moat rather than eroding it; Columbia Threadneedle turns net-inflow positive as its above-target margin funds competitive fee compression; equity markets continue a multi-year bull run lifting AUM/AUA broadly. Revenue grows 10% year 1 fading to a 5% terminal rate, roughly matching the trailing 5-year CAGR sustained rather than decelerating.
bull.margin_rationale: Pretax margin expands from 26.5% to 28.0% as Columbia Threadneedle's margin outperformance (43-44% vs 35-39% target) broadens and AWM's record productivity (+12% YoY) keeps cost growth below revenue growth even through the Huntington transition; +1.1% SBC add-back.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NI margin (~21.8% mature) x g / ROE(53%): higher growth needs more capital even at a better return, but the higher ROE keeps the distributed share above 90% throughout.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 30% and bull cut to 20%: AMP's revenue is structurally asset/market-linked (wrap and AUM fees) on top of an already-flagged deceleration in organic net inflows (AWM -59% YoY in Q1-26) and persistent Columbia Threadneedle net outflows, so the base case already embeds meaningful flow headwinds and a market correction would compound rather than merely offset them -- a genuinely adverse combination (recruiting losses + slipped Huntington timeline + market drawdown) is a real near-term risk, not a remote tail. Bull is cut because it requires sustained double-digit growth AND further margin expansion AND continued market tailwinds to all hold simultaneously for a decade, a higher bar than the base case's already-optimistic assumption that Huntington fully offsets Comerica on schedule.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
